intro.title: Build race condition safe search UI
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a search input component that safely handles user typing without showing outdated results. You will learn how race conditions occur when fast user input triggers multiple asynchronous search calls that may return out of order. The core concept is using JavaScript's AbortController to cancel previous requests when a new one is made, ensuring only the latest search results are displayed. You will implement this with React state hooks and event handlers to create a responsive, error-free UI. By the end, you'll have a practical understanding of managing asynchronous operations in a real-world front-end scenario.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for search interfaces in e-commerce platforms like Amazon or travel sites like Booking.com, where users rapidly type queries while the system fetches results. It prevents outdated search results from overwriting newer ones when network responses arrive out of order. Developers implement this in dashboard filters, admin panels with live data, and any autocomplete field where API calls must be canceled or ignored if stale. Without race condition handling, users see incorrect data that damages trust and usability.
